key_insight: A budget-aware uncertainty-driven QA framework built on nnU-Net ranks regions by predicted uncertainty so clinicians can review a small, prioritized subset and catch most segmentation errors with minimal manual effort.
problem_solved: Reduces the time and risk of manual Clinical Target Volume (CTV) correction in radiotherapy by providing reliable cues about where auto-segmentation (especially for complex TMLI cases) is likely to be wrong and should be inspected first.
method: Estimate model uncertainty from nnU-Net segmentation outputs to localize likely errors.
Translate uncertainty into a budget-aware ranking/prioritization scheme that selects slices/regions for manual QA under a fixed review time or slice budget.
Evaluate trade-offs between review budget and error detection on TMLI cases to quantify saved effort versus missed errors.
impact: Enables safer, more efficient clinical deployment of auto-segmentation by directing limited QA resources where they matter most; practitioners can tune review budgets to desired safety/efficiency trade-offs.
visual_elements: Pipeline flowchart: nnU-Net → uncertainty estimation → budget-aware prioritization → clinician review
Budget vs. error-detection curve (recall or IoU loss found vs. percent slices reviewed)
CT slices with overlay heatmap showing uncertainty and highlighted slices selected for review
Bar chart showing manual time saved versus residual segmentation errors across budgets
paper_title: Budget-Aware Uncertainty for Radiotherapy Segmentation QA Using nnU-Net
paper_authors: Ricardo Coimbra Brioso, Lorenzo Mondo, Damiano Dei, Nicola Lambri, Pietro Mancosu
